title: Gene counts per cell
methods:
**Data.** The cohort's 10x datasets, each from its FASTQs on its own 2024-A reference (GRCh38, GRCm39 or the human+mouse barnyard): PBMC 3' v3 and v2, mouse neurons and nuclei, the barnyard, PBMC with antibodies, and 5' PBMC (first 60 M read pairs). The same FASTQs and GTF feed Singlet, STARsolo and alevin-fry.

**Cells and genes.** Cells are the barcodes STARsolo EmptyDrops_CR calls, so the cell set does not depend on Singlet. A family is compared on the cells all its tools have and the genes all of them annotate (Ensembl ids).

**Families.** Exonic UMI: Singlet exon_counts (spliced + ambiguous), STARsolo Gene, and the Cell Ranger matrix 10x published. Exon+intron UMI: Singlet exon+intron, STARsolo GeneFull, alevin-fry USA (S+U+A).

**Measures, for every pair of tools.** The distance of the median per-cell UMI ratio from 1 (|ln ratio|); the median over cells of the Pearson r of log1p counts over genes; the Spearman rho of pseudobulk gene counts.

**Gate.** Singlet's mean value against its competitors must be as good as the competitors' value against each other, within the half-width of the paired bootstrap 95% CI of the difference. Singlet is gated as a member of the cloud of existing tools, not as better than each. Per-reference values are in each metric's notes. With one competitor (5' Cell Ranger) the threshold comes from the other datasets.

**Real truth.** pbmc1k_cite_v3 has antibody counts for the same cells: Spearman across cells between each protein and its coding gene, per tool.

**Not compared.** scBaseCount: the 10x demo datasets are not in SRA, and the Kang lane is 3' v1, a chemistry scBaseCount does not process, so no equal-depth comparison exists.

tools.name: singlet
tools.params: singlet encode --reads R1.fastq.gz R2.fastq.gz -o s.1fq; singlet s.1fq --ref-base $REF --genome-dir $REF/$SPECIES/star_2.7.11b --exons $REF/$SPECIES/genes/genes.gtf --out-prefix $OUT/ --threads 8 --pipeline --output-format mtx --raw-matrix

tools.name: starsolo-gene
tools.citation: Kaminow, Yunusov, Dobin. STARsolo: accurate, fast and versatile mapping/quantification of single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq data. bioRxiv 2021
tools.params: STAR --runThreadN 16 --genomeDir $GENOME --readFilesIn $R2 $R1 --readFilesCommand zcat --soloType CB_UMI_Simple --soloCBwhitelist $WHITELIST --soloCBlen 16 --soloUMIstart 17 --soloUMIlen $UMILEN --soloBarcodeReadLength 0 --soloStrand $STRAND --soloFeatures Gene GeneFull Velocyto SJ --soloCellFilter EmptyDrops_CR --soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts --soloUMIfiltering MultiGeneUMI_CR --soloUMIdedup 1MM_CR --clipAdapterType CellRanger4 --outFilterScoreMin 30 --outSAMtype None (the STARsolo manual's Cell Ranger 4+ emulation; $UMILEN 12 for v3, 10 for v2 and 5'; $STRAND Forward, Reverse for 5')

tools.name: starsolo-genefull
tools.params: same STARsolo run as starsolo-gene; feature GeneFull (exons + introns)

tools.name: alevin-fry-usa
tools.citation: He et al. Alevin-fry unlocks rapid, accurate and memory-frugal quantification of single-cell RNA-seq data. Nat Methods 2022
tools.params: simpleaf quant --reads1 $R1 --reads2 $R2 --index af_idx/index --t2g-map af_idx/index/t2g_3col.tsv --chemistry $CHEM(10xv3|10xv2|10xv2-5p) --expected-ori fw --resolution cr-like --unfiltered-pl $WHITELIST --threads 16; index: simpleaf index --ref-type spliced+unspliced --rlen 91 on the same FASTA and GTF

tools.name: cellranger-published
tools.params: Cell Ranger is not run. Comparator = the filtered matrix 10x publishes with each dataset (10x reference of the time, not 2024-A): pbmc1k_v3: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v3/pbmc_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5; pbmc1k_v2: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v2/pbmc_1k_v2_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5; neuron1k_v3: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/neuron_1k_v3/neuron_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5; hgmm1k_v3: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/hgmm_1k_v3/hgmm_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5; pbmc1k_cite_v3: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_protein_v3/pbmc_1k_protein_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5; nuclei2k_v2: Cell Ranger 2.1.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/2.1.0/nuclei_2k/nuclei_2k_filtered_gene_bc_matrices.tar.gz; pbmc5p_v1: Cell Ranger 3.0.0 https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-vdj/3.0.0/vdj_v1_hs_pbmc2_5gex_protein/vdj_v1_hs_pbmc2_5gex_protein_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5

metrics.name: Per-cell UMI total, distance of the median ratio from 1, exonic UMI

rule.rationale: gate = Singlet's mean |ln ratio| distance to STARsolo Gene, Cell Ranger (published) against the distance the competitors have from each other (0.0391); tolerance = half-width of the paired bootstrap 95% CI of the difference: 0.0004

metrics.notes: Singlet vs each competitor (S/competitor for ratios): STARsolo Gene: ratio 0.992; Cell Ranger (published): ratio 1.031. Basis: cells with UMI in every tool (1220). Competitor value = its mean distance to the other competitors.

metrics.name: Per-cell gene correlation, exonic UMI

rule.rationale: gate = Singlet's mean r distance to STARsolo Gene, Cell Ranger (published) against the distance the competitors have from each other (0.9818); tolerance = half-width of the paired bootstrap 95% CI of the difference: 0.0001

metrics.notes: Singlet vs each competitor (S/competitor for ratios): STARsolo Gene: 0.9939; Cell Ranger (published): 0.9793. Basis: cells common to the family. Competitor value = its mean distance to the other competitors.

caveats: Cell Ranger is the matrix 10x published with each dataset (versions 2.1.0 and 3.0.0, 10x references of the time, exonic UMIs), not a re-run on the 2024-A reference, so its comparisons also carry reference and annotation differences.

The 5' dataset is the first 60 M read pairs, so the published full-depth Cell Ranger matrix is left out for it; that dataset's exonic gate is a threshold borrowed from the other datasets, not a measured spread.

There is no ground truth for counts: every metric is agreement between tools, and the tolerance is the spread between the competitors. A tool can sit inside that spread and still be wrong where the competitors are.

The gate averages Singlet's distance to its competitors. It is looser than requiring Singlet to be at least as close to each competitor separately; the per-reference values are in the notes of each metric. Tool settings were fixed before any metric was computed and no Singlet parameter was tuned on these data.
Singlet's exon+intron definition counts reads that STARsolo GeneFull discards (reads overlapping two gene bodies), so totals above 1 against GeneFull are expected.
Wall time and memory in resources are from a shared cluster at differing thread counts (Singlet 8, STARsolo and alevin-fry 16) and are not a speed comparison.

Cohort datasets assigned to gex-counts that this document does not cover (no run for them in this benchmark yet): pbmc5k_v4_d1, pbmc10k_5p_v2, mouse_brain_nuclei5k_v31, pbmc_multiome10k, pbmc10k_cite_v3, macosko2015_dropseq_mix, tenx_crispr_a375_10k, norman2019_gem1, tenx_crispr_a549_5k, visium_mouse_brain_ant, ding2020_pbmc1_smartseq2, ding2020_pbmc1_dropseq, ding2020_pbmc1_indrops, ding2020_pbmc1_seqwell, ding2020_pbmc1_celseq2, ding2020_pbmc1_10xv3, segerstolpe2016_pancreas, heart1k_v3, tabula_muris_kidney_facs, gsm5815984.
conclusion: On 7 datasets (3' v2 and v3, 5', nuclei, mouse, barnyard), Singlet's exonic UMI per cell is 0.98-1.02 of STARsolo Gene's (median ratio; gene correlation 0.962-0.994). Exon+intron counts are 1.02-1.10 of STARsolo GeneFull's (r 0.948-0.987) and 0.92-1.03 of alevin-fry USA's. 36 of 44 gating metrics pass: Singlet sits inside the spread of the competitors, except 8 metrics (see metrics).
